title: Semi-Markovian switching in a fluctuating harmonic trap: An age-structured formulation
abstract: We study a Brownian particle in a harmonic trap whose stiffness switches between two values with arbitrary waiting-time statistics, generating semi-Markovian dynamics. To treat the resulting temporal memory, we formulate the problem in an enlarged age-structured state space, restoring Markovianity and yielding a local Fokker--Planck description. Within this framework, we derive exact steady-state integral equations for the spatial and birth distributions and obtain exact expressions for stationary moments, injected power, and potential energy. In the second part of the paper, we analyze the stochastic-resetting limit, corresponding to a particle alternately released and trapped. By representing the stationary spatial distribution as a superposition of Gaussian states with fluctuating variance, the problem can be reformulated as a switching process in variance space. This yields exact integral equations for the variance distributions and leads to a simplified description amenable to direct analytical treatment.
summary: This paper develops an advanced framework using age-structured and variance-space methods to study Brownian motion in a harmonic trap whose stiffness switches semi-Markovianly. It shows that while the average potential energy remains at equilibrium, the system's injected power and spatial fluctuations are acutely sensitive to the memory encoded in the switching waiting times. This provides powerful tools for analyzing non-equilibrium steady states driven by complex temporal correlations.
main_problem: The study investigates non-equilibrium dynamics of a Brownian particle whose confining harmonic trap stiffness switches stochastically between two values with arbitrary waiting-time statistics.
main_result: The authors derive exact integral equations for the steady state, showing that while potential energy remains at equilibrium, injected power and spatial fluctuations are highly sensitive to the memory encoded in the switching statistics.
method: The problem is tackled first using an enlarged age-structured Fokker-Planck formulation to restore Markovianity, followed by a transformation into a deterministic evolution equation within variance space for the stochastic-resetting limit.
model_or_system: A single Brownian particle confined by a harmonic potential $u(x) =  rac{1}{2}Kx^2$, where the stiffness $K$ switches between two values ($K_1, K_2$) according to arbitrary waiting-time statistics. The dynamics are analyzed in both position space and an enlarged age-structured state space.

important_parameters: The stiffness values ($K_1, K_2$), mean residence times ($	au_i$), and the nature of the waiting-time statistics (e.g., exponential vs. algebraic tails).
main_assumptions: The spatial dynamics between switches are assumed to remain locally Brownian; for steady state analysis, finite mean residence times ($	au_i < \infty$) are required.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the variance distributions $\pi(s)$ for different switching protocols (e.g., exponential vs. deterministic) and show how confinement suppresses large-variance fluctuations relative to the released state.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general age-structured framework for semi-Markovian dynamics, deriving steady-state integral equations for moments. It then analyzes the stochastic-resetting limit by transforming the problem into variance space, yielding simplified integral equations and asymptotic results based on waiting-time tail behavior.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical tool (age-structured/variance-space formalism) to analyze non-equilibrium energy dissipation in systems driven by colored noise or switching potentials, which is highly relevant for understanding active matter or fluctuating quantum environments.
